parent_source: MetaWeft 1abb3419b94106b9c413575d72f372206af86d53, src/ace_adapt_reme_task and experiment/appworld integration, plus pre-existing working changes to accounting and experiment documentation. V2 shares the parent's task-memory implementation, framework contracts, services, retrieval and AppWorld executor/loader/evaluator/logger. Prompt lineage records the actual parent bytes and transformations. Every run copies the working implementation and sibling dependencies; the captured source is the recoverable execution record.
hypothesis: Supplying memory content without bookkeeping and learning adaptation rules only from successful adapter input/output pairs may reduce context waste and task-knowledge drift in the adaptation playbook. This combined comparison establishes operability in the smoke, not improved task performance.
intended_differences: A separate V2 entrypoint preserves V1. Adapter inputs contain task-memory content strings and playbook content grouped under memory_selection, task_specific_pruning and exploration_guidance; canonical IDs and source references stay in artifacts. Adaptation updates require official scalar reward exactly 1 and a valid completed adapter call. Their model input is the saved adapter input and validated output, with only the edit revision and target lookup needed for ADD/UPDATE bookkeeping; no execution trajectory or evaluator details. Rewritten adapter/update prompts teach adaptation operations rather than domain procedures.
memory_structure: Task-memory schema remains metaweft-task-memory-v1: named ReMe-like records, applicability, content, source references and complete embeddings. Adaptation memory uses metaweft-adaptation-memory-v2 with schema_version 2, stable IDs, revision/counter, content and source references, grouped into memory selection, task-specific pruning and exploration guidance. Stored metadata remains available for audit and localized updates.
retrieval: Unchanged shared efficiency_1 retrieval with final k=10, combined-vector HNSW depth 20, 40 ANN candidates, RRF constant 20, candidate limit 20 and qwen3.8-flash listwise ranking to 20. Small pools bypass ranking; empty task memory makes no retrieval embedding call. Adaptation sees the full playbook; no playbook retrieval, truncation or compression.
adaptation: One temperature-zero call on every task, including both-empty initialization. It selects useful memory content, prunes irrelevant task details and identifies missing information with concrete exploration guidance. It returns exactly a JSON guidance string, supplied once to the executor. Preserve the exact request, raw response, validated output, prompt hashes and canonical call references separately from prompt content.
execution_context: Unchanged fixed-guide AppWorld ReAct execution: qwen3.8-flash, temperature 0.9, seed 0, thinking disabled, at most 40 interactions, one trial and AppWorld seed 100. No within-task memory refresh. Embeddings use text-embedding-3-large at 1024 dimensions. Timeouts and provider retry policy are inherited and recorded per run.
evidence_update: Task memory continues to learn from both successes and failures using the parent's frozen episode and add/skip/revise/defer consolidation. Adaptation memory updates only after reward == 1.0 and schema-valid completed adaptation; other outcomes are explicit non-degraded skips with no update call. Its input/output evidence supports reusable selection, pruning and exploration rules, without trajectory evidence or causal claims from success alone. Validate ADD/UPDATE batches atomically; preserve before-images, applied-edit references and unrelated entries. Empty edits do not change revision.
feedback_access: Success gating uses only official scalar reward in code. The adapter sees whitelisted current task information plus memory content. The adaptation updater sees the actual sanitized adapter input, validated guide and minimal edit targeting, and cannot see trajectory, scalar score, evaluator assertions, reference solutions or newly changed task memory. Task-memory update feedback access remains V1's sanitized trace and scalar reward. Full evidence remains in run artifacts outside adaptation-update prompts.
memory_lifetime: Both memories start empty independently per invocation/split, persist across the ordered task stream and update before the next task. Every completed task advances the committed pair epoch, including adaptation skips and no-ops. Writable memory, benchmark state, checkpoints and output are isolated. Shared completed response store remains the exception; no_cache is the default. No warm-start interface or task parallelism within a split.
failure_reporting: Preserve branch outcomes, canonical call accounting and degraded schema failures. Exhausted provider/cache calls, logging/artifact errors, uncertain writes and required snapshot failures prevent task commit. Keep the existing prompt byte guard and no structured-output repair policy. A policy skip is distinct from degraded model output; missing usage remains unknown.
recovery_protocol: Checkpoint format 2 commits both memory snapshots and task position atomically. V2 adaptation snapshots identify schema v2 and use its validator/renderer; task snapshots remain schema v1. Recovery restores a coherent pair from captured source/settings into a fresh isolated run and skips all committed-task work. Setting and identity checks prevent V1/V2 cross-recovery. Existing V1 and format-1 settings retain their contracts.
comparison: Compare against metaweft_v1 with matched task order, empty initialization, models, budgets, cache policy and retrieval. The requested two-case smoke checks behavior only; no extra baseline run or autonomous design search is included.
